subject: Shiny helps win prize at NHS Hackday, UK - and file-upload request.

messages.author: 81b6b3d7dfea88a5
messages.subject: Shiny helps win prize at NHS Hackday, UK - and file-upload request.
parts:
Hello to the Shiny team,

Firstly a big thankyou. I used Shiny and my own package rworldmap to create a small GUI visualizing health service administration areas as a part of NHSHackday at the weekend (see nhshackday.com). It helped me win a t-shirt, hurrah! Without shiny I wouldn't have been able to create something as useful in a day and a halfs coding.

To see the tidied entry :
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/southandy/nhsAdminAreasGUI4new/

I think the main thing the judges liked was that it allows users to upload any relevant data that they have, join it to the map, and visualise it.

The only problem is that file uploading appears not to be working on glimmer now. See https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/BSSQqTJM0gs

So I'm sure you are busy but I'd just like to add a vote for fixing that when you can.

All the best,
Andy

parts:
Hi Amy,

Thanks, happy to share. I haven't found the time to get to grips with github yet (will soon) so here's the code :

UI.r
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  # Application title
  headerPanel("CCGsee : for viewing Clinical Commissioning Group data"),
  
  # Sidebar with controls 
  sidebarPanel(
    
    uiOutput("choose_dataset"),

    selectInput("regionToPlot", "Plot which region ?",
                c("England" = "England",
                  "North" = "North",
                  "South" = "South",
                  "London" = "London",
                  "Midlands and East" = "Midlands and East"
                )),    
    
    checkboxInput("addLegend", "add Legend to maps", TRUE), #var,name

    checkboxInput("addCodes", "add CCG codes to maps", FALSE), #var,name
    
    fileInput("file", "Load CCG data from a csv (must have CCG codes in column called CCG.code)", multiple=FALSE)
  ),
  
  
  mainPanel(
    
    h5("made at NHS HackDay Oxford 2013 by Andy South, Barry Rowlingson, Chris Martin and Rob Aldridge"),
    h5("contact sout...@gmail.com"),
    
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Map", plotOutput("mapPlot")),
      tabPanel("Bubble Map", plotOutput("mapBubblesPlot")),      
      tabPanel("Table", tableOutput("tablePlot")),
      tabPanel("Uploaded attribute data", tableOutput("filetable"))
      #tabPanel("demo Zoom map", includeHTML("olayer.html"))      
    ) # end of tabsetPanel
        
  )
))

server.r
library(shiny)
library(rworldmap)

#load the data stored as files in the app folder
load('sPDF_CCG2.rda')


shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 
  #for Barrys openLayers tab
  #addResourcePath("maps","maps")

  #creating a reactive variable for the map+data
  #so that whenever it is changed anything using it updates
  v <- reactiveValues( sPDF_CCGlocal = sPDF_CCG2 )
  
  
  # Drop-down selection box for columns
  output$choose_dataset <- reactiveUI(function() {  
    
    selectInput("attributeToPlot", "Plot which attribute of CCGs ?", choices=getColumnNames())                  
  })

  
  # to provide a list of selected species based on input parameter
  getColumnNames <- reactive( function() {  
    
    as.character( names(v$sPDF_CCGlocal)[c(3:ncol(v$sPDF_CCGlocal))])    
    })   

  #creating a command string for map plotting
  formulaText <- reactive(function() {
    
    trueOrFalse <- "FALSE"
    if (input$addLegend) trueOrFalse <- "TRUE"
 
    textOut <- paste("mapPolys(sPDF, nameColumnToPlot='",input$attributeToPlot,"', addLegend=",trueOrFalse,")",sep='') #, mapTitle=''   
    
    if (input$addCodes)
    {
      textAdd <- "\ntext( coordinates(sPDF), sPDF$CCG.code, cex=0.8 )"
      textOut <- paste(textOut,textAdd)
    }
    
    if ( input$regionToPlot != 'England' )
    {    
      textAdd <- paste("sPDF <- sPDF[ which(sPDF$Region =='", input$regionToPlot,"'), ]\n", sep='')
      textOut <- paste(textAdd, textOut)
    }
    
    textOut 
    }) # end of formulaText()

  
  # Return the formula text for printing as a caption
  output$caption <- reactiveText(function() {
    formulaText()
  })
  
  # Generate a plot 
  output$mapPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
 
    if( length(input$attributeToPlot) == 0 )
    {
      plot.new()
      mtext("please wait for map to load (~20 seconds)",cex=2,col='purple')
    }  
    
    #to stop it trying to plot map before an option has been chosen
    if( length(input$attributeToPlot) > 0 )
    { 
      sPDF <- v$sPDF_CCGlocal
      
      oldpar <- par(mar=c(4,0,1,0)) # bottom, left, top, right  
      eval(parse(text=formulaText()))
      
      mtext("map made using rworldmap", line=-2, side=1, adj=0, cex=0.8, col='purple')
      
      par(oldpar)
    }
      
  }) #end of mapPlot
 
  
  # bubble plot 
  output$mapBubblesPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
     
    sPDF <- v$sPDF_CCGlocal
    
    if ( input$regionToPlot != 'England' )
    {     
      sPDF <- sPDF[ which(sPDF$Region == input$regionToPlot),]     
    }
    
    oldpar <- par(mar=c(0,0,0,0)) # no gap therefore no room for axis
    mapBubbles(sPDF, nameZSize=input$attributeToPlot, fill=FALSE )
    
    if (input$addCodes)
    {
      text( coordinates(sPDF), sPDF$CCG.code, cex=0.8 )
    }  
    
    mtext("map made using rworldmap", line=-2, side=1, adj=0, cex=0.8, col='purple')
    
    par(oldpar)
  }) #end of mapBubblesPlot 

  
  # table
  output$tablePlot <- reactiveTable(function() {
    
    sPDF <- v$sPDF_CCGlocal
    
    if ( input$regionToPlot != 'England' )
    {     
      sPDF <- sPDF[ which(sPDF$Region == input$regionToPlot),]     
    }
    
    sPDF@data    
  }) #end of tablePlot 

  
  #called when user uploads a file
  output$filetable <- reactiveTable(function() {
    
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }   
    
    #cat("input$file=",input$file)
    print(paste("input$file$datapath=",input$file$datapath))    
    
    dFuserData <- read.csv(input$file$datapath)
    
    #join data onto the map (changing the global sPDF in this function)
    #WEHAY! the isolate stops the reactive variable from setting up an infinite reactivity loop !
    sPDF_CCG3 <- joinData2Map(dF=dFuserData, nameMap=isolate(v$sPDF_CCGlocal), nameJoinIDMap='CCG.code', nameJoinColumnData='CCG.code')
    
    v$sPDF_CCGlocal <- sPDF_CCG3
           
    #what to print in the table
    dFuserData #just the user data
    
    #isolate stops an infinite loop
    #isolate(v$sPDF_CCGlocal@data) #the user data joined to the map attribute data
    
  }) # end of filetable 
  
})
